newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-David Jones shares continue to slide.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-David Jones shares continue to slide.

text.p: Shares in upmarket retailer, David Jones Ltd, continued to slide in early Monday trade, losing a further 7.2 percent to a 15 week low of A$1.55 after Friday's warning of a 50 percent cut in first half net profit.

The upmarket department store operator said on Friday it had lowered its first half net profit forecast by up to 50 percent due to lower revenues and higher depreciation charges with manging director Chris Tideman pointing to a lacklustre retail trading environment, despite good Christmas week trading.
The company said the lower sales and profits could also affect its dividend policy which was currently being revised.

"With the profit falling as much as it has, it is going to put the dividend under increasing pressure and people are very much dividend-conscious at the moment," said a Brisbane-based dealer, adding that the poor outlook for the sector may prompt analysts to reconsider their forecasts.

"Retail has found it fairly competitive going and that outlook is likely to remain in place over the next six months. This poor result coming out so early may have alerted analysts to the sector and they are probably having a closer look at some
By 12.00 p.m. (0100 GMT), David Jones shares were 12 cents lower at A$1.55 on turnover of 1,247,899 shares.
